messages:
tara: FYI customer reported strangely high billing after intermittent network blip. looks like a streaming truncate + retry caused both provisional and final charges to land. thread to decide patch.

lin: can you paste the session id and the billing entries? rough numbers help.

tara: sess=sd_92a3; provisional billed 120 tokens at 12:03:15 when runtime did a soft-truncate. client reconnected and resumed; runtime trimmed an extra 10 tokens on replay so final confirmed charge was 110 at 12:03:47. customer saw 230 billed.

tara: snippets:
```
[frontend] client disconnected conn=abc
[runtime] soft_truncate sess=sd_92a3 provisional_tokens=120 snapshot_id=snap_7
[billing] provisional acct=ac_900 tx=tx_p1 tokens=120
[router] reconnect conn=def sess=sd_92a3 replay=true
[runtime] execute toolcall tool=tc_9 produced_tokens=110
[billing] confirmed acct=ac_900 tx=tx_p2 tokens=110
```

kevin: so same flow as other incidents but two differences: 1) final confirmed token count is less (120 vs 110) — indicates truncation differences on replay; 2) router marked replay but we don't currently forward any original snapshot id or provisional tx id to billing. Billing treats provisional and confirmed as independent.

mike: any chance provisional was supposed to be voided when confirmed arrives? we don't have a link between provisional row and confirmed row currently. console can't do automatic reconciliation.

lin: quick mitigation options: A) billing-side squash rule: if final_confirmed and provisional_overlap(session) -> reconcile and keep whichever is max (or prefer provisional). B) router -> attach snapshot_id and replay flag so billing can reconcile deterministically. C) console -> surface provisional vs confirmed and auto-suggest refunds.

kevin: adding replay flag to telemetry is cheap and helpful. But durable solution is for router to forward the original snapshot_id or toolcall id so billing can do exact matching. Otherwise billing fuzzy heuristics will be messy and might false-positive.

billing-bot: Created ticket BILL-1277 "reconcile provisional vs confirmed charges on stream replays" assigned to @mike.

ops-bot: Incident INC-8021 logged; tags: routing,billing,console,l2-sre.

tara: can we also add a short audit entry when billing marks provisional? e.g., billing stores provisional_pointer = snapshot_id so later confirms can reference it. That would require router -> runtime -> billing chain to include the snapshot_id.

mike: agree. Plan: 1) immediate: console visual flag for provisional rows + hover text and a "reconcile suggestion" button (1d) 2) short-term: emit replay/reconnect telemetry and add `snapshot_id` passthrough in router (2d) 3) billing changes: accept `snapshot_id` on confirm and atomically reconcile provisional row (3d).

console-dev: I can do the UI flag in a day; will add a warning and a button that opens BILL-1277. We should include the raw tx ids to make refunds trivial.

lin: acceptance test: simulate soft-truncate provisional -> reconnect with replay that produces fewer tokens -> assert ledger net charge equals max(prov, confirmed) after reconcile flow OR equals provisional if we decide that policy. Need to pick policy now.

kevin: policy debate: prefer provisional (higher) or prefer confirmed (actual executed)? I vote for prefer provisional because customers saw provisional consumed and may have assumed those tokens were used; but that might overcharge if confirm is much lower. Another option: prefer confirmed but refund provisional delta automatically. That sounds fairer.

mike: prefer confirmed + auto-refund provisional delta. operationally we can mark provisional replaced_by=tx_confirm and create refund tx that is traceable.

tara: +1 confirmed + refund. we'll need guardrails to avoid refund churn with flapping reconnects. maybe only allow one reconciliation per snapshot within 5 minutes.

lin: telemetry: add tag reconcile_attempt=true and reconcile_outcome={kept_confirmed,kept_provisional,manual_refund}. helps ops dashboards.

kevin: small caveat: toolcalls can be non-idempotent. if runtime actually re-executed a toolcall and it had side effects, customer might expect to be charged for both. We must distinguish replay that reuses cached outputs vs fresh execution. runtime needs to annotate whether toolcall was a cache-hit/kv-restored or actually re-run. add `execution_kind=cache|replay|fresh` to telemetry.

mike: noted. billing will only auto-refund when execution_kind!=fresh (or when we can prove idempotent). Put that in BILL-1277.

ops-bot: Added note to INC-8021: "ensure reconciliation only auto-refunds when execution_kind != fresh".

console-dev: UI will show execution_kind in expanded ledger row if available. Also adding quick filter "replay incidents".

tara: I'll contact the customer with proposed refund policy (prefer confirmed + auto-refund provisional delta when toolcall was not fresh). We should run a small backfill to find how many accounts would be impacted.

mike: owners: router passthrough & telemetry -> @kevin; billing reconcile + refund logic -> @mike; console flag + filter -> @console-dev; SRE to monitor -> @tara. I'll update BILL-1277 with tasks and risk notes.

kevin: starting router patch today, will add `x-snapshot-id`, `x-replay` headers and `execution_kind` telemetry.

tara: thanks all. ping here when PRs are ready. :slightly_smiling_face:
